steps.notes: Gold passes; my independent attractive-gravity (N,3) impl passes. Description text contradicts docstring/target on BOTH force sign and array shape (see findings).
Gold and my impl pass — but so do zero-acceleration, sign-flipped, and forgot-mass-division implementations: all target accelerations are below np.allclose atol (see finding).
Gold and my impl pass — but forward Euler and a no-gravity integrator also pass: the RK4 requirement is unconstrained by these targets (see finding).

Gold and my round((t1-t0)/dt) impl pass all 4 tests incl. the Sun-Earth energy-conservation bool test. But a correct-physics correct-RK4 solver using the common accumulate while-loop fails tests 1-2 (extra step from float dt), and RK2 passes everything (see findings).

findings.evidence: Both prompt formulas have the gravitational force sign INVERTED (repulsive) relative to the target. Description: 'F_{i,j} = -G m_i m_j \frac{\vec{r}_j - \vec{r}_i }{|\vec{r}_i - \vec{r}_j|^3}' — under the standard reading (F_{i,j} = force on i due to j) this points AWAY from j. Background is unambiguous: 'F_1 = - (G m_1 m_2 / r^2) (r/r)' where 'r/r is the unit vector pointing from mass m_1 to mass m_2' — i.e. the force on m_1 points away from m_2 (repulsion). The h5 target encodes ATTRACTION: test 0 (particles at x=0 and x=1) target f[0] = [+0.0066743, 0, 0], pointing from particle 0 toward particle 1; gold code computes f[i] = -G*sum((r_i-r_j)*m_i*m_j/r^3) = attraction. Probe review/work/49/probe_repulsive.py (literal implementation of the stated formula) FAILS step 49.1 official joint scoring. A solver is scored correct only if it overrides the prompt's explicit formula with outside domain knowledge.
findings.suggested_fix: Fix the sign in both texts: description F_{i,j} = +G m_i m_j (r_j - r_i)/|r_i - r_j|^3 (force on i due to j), background F_1 = +(G m_1 m_2 / r^2) r_hat with r_hat pointing from m_1 to m_2.

findings.evidence: Description vs docstring shape contradiction. Description: 'The function shall take as input the current location of the particles as a 1D array xin of size $3*N$ ... The output is the 1D array of forces acting on each particles also as a $3*N$ length array.' Header docstring: 'xin: 2D array of locations for the N particles, N,3 elements' / 'f: 2D array of forces, on each particle, N,3 elements'. Tests pass 2D (N,3) inputs and h5 targets are (N,3). Probe review/work/49/probe_1d_literal.py (correct physics, returns the description's 1D 3*N array) FAILS officially with 'ValueError: operands could not be broadcast together with shapes (6,) (2,3)'. The docstring disambiguates for solvers who prioritize it, but the primary task text explicitly specifies a contract that cannot pass.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite the description sentence to match the docstring: input is a 2D array xin of shape (N,3); output f is a 2D array of shape (N,3).

findings.evidence: All acceleration components of all three targets are below np.allclose's default atol=1e-8 (max |a| = 1.197e-9; most are 1e-10..1e-12), because tests use O(1) masses with G=6.6743e-11. Therefore the entire physics content of the step — Newton's second law, the call to Nbody_Fij, the division by mass, even the SIGN of gravity — is unconstrained; only the trivial rhs[:,0:3]=uin[:,3:6] velocity copy is tested. Probes (all PASS official joint scoring): probe_zero_accel.py (rhs[:,3:6]=0, gravity ignored entirely), probe_repulsive_rhs.py (sign-flipped repulsive gravity), probe_forgot_mass.py (acceleration=force, mass division forgotten). Pattern: 'Target magnitude vs atol'.
findings.suggested_fix: Use test masses large enough that accelerations are O(1) (e.g. masses ~1e10, as 49.1's tests do for forces), or state G=1 units, or assert with an explicit atol of 0 / a scaled tolerance.

findings.evidence: Same root cause as 49.2: with O(1) masses, accelerations are ~1e-10, so a single RK4 step is indistinguishable from free streaming (x+v*dt) at default tolerance — the gravity correction to position is ~0.5*a*dt^2 ~ 1e-13 and the velocity targets equal the input velocities to all printed digits. Probes that PASS official joint scoring: probe_euler.py (forward Euler instead of RK4, correct gravity) and probe_nograv_full.py (RK4 structure with zero gravity). The step's named requirement — the classical 4th-order Runge-Kutta combination — is not verified by any of its three tests.
findings.suggested_fix: Use masses/positions giving O(1) accelerations (or G=1 units) so that k1..k4 differ measurably and Euler/RK2/no-gravity implementations fail.

findings.evidence: The prompt says only 'integrating using a fixed step sized dt starting from t0 and ending at t1'; it never specifies how to derive the step count, and tests 1-2 use dt values (0.3, 0.15) that are not exactly representable in binary. (60-30)/0.3 and 600/0.15 happen to evaluate to exactly 100.0 and 4000.0, so int/round/ceil all work, but the very common accumulate loop 't=t0; while t<t1: u=RK4(u); t+=dt' takes 101 and 4001 steps (30+100*0.3 accumulates to 59.99999999999998<60). Probe review/work/49/probe_whileloop.py — correct attractive gravity, correct RK4, this loop — FAILS official joint scoring (isolated: tests 1 and 2 fail, position error ~v*dt~0.27 >> rtol*|target|; tests 0 and 3 pass). Gold itself uses Nsteps=int(np.ceil((t1-t0)/dt)), which only coincidentally agrees with round() on these inputs. A solver with fully correct physics and integrator is failed purely on float endpoint handling.
findings.suggested_fix: Either state explicitly 'take exactly round((t1-t0)/dt) steps' in the prompt/docstring, or choose dt values that are exactly representable and divide (t1-t0) exactly (e.g. 0.25, 0.3125).

findings.evidence: Position/velocity tests 0-2 are gravity-insensitive: probe_nograv_full.py (no gravity at all) passes tests 0-2 under --isolate (3/4) and is caught ONLY by test 3's Sun-Earth energy-conservation bool (official joint verdict correctly FAIL). Test 3 in turn checks only conservation, not trajectory or order of accuracy: probe_rk2_full.py (midpoint RK2 instead of RK4) PASSES the entire step officially (forward Euler is caught, energy drift ~5e-3 rel > isclose rtol). Net effect: nowhere in the whole problem is 4th-order accuracy actually verified, and gravity itself is verified only by 49.1 and 49.4-test-3. Also noted: test 3's helper Nbody_Etot uses Epot = -2*G*m_i*m_j/r (factor 2 vs the physical pairwise potential, flagged 'this is horrible' in the test's own comment) — harmless for a conservation check but a data smell.
findings.suggested_fix: Add at least one test where gravity visibly bends trajectories at default tolerance (e.g. Sun-Earth positions after 1 year compared against the frozen RK4 result), which would also separate RK2 from RK4 at suitable dt.

overall_assessment: Gold passes all 4 steps and a competent solver who knows gravity is attractive, follows the docstring shapes, and computes the step count as round((t1-t0)/dt) passes everything. However the problem has serious calibration defects on both sides: (1) the prompt's force formulas are sign-inverted (repulsive) and 49.1's description specifies 1D I/O while the scored contract is 2D — literal readings fail; (2) steps 49.2 and 49.3 are nearly vacuous because O(1) test masses with SI G push all accelerations below np.allclose's atol, so no-gravity / wrong-sign / Euler implementations earn credit for those steps; (3) 49.4's dt=0.3/0.15 choices fail correct implementations that use the common accumulate while-loop. Fair scoring as-is is questionable: the step-level scores for 49.2/49.3 measure only array bookkeeping, and 49.1/49.4 can fail correct-physics solvers on prompt-text and float-endpoint traps.
